verdict.line: You lose when you force Q all-ins into an up Feint; you win when you poke with E and double-cast W until your items spike.

brief.thesis: Shen's kit is built to deny the exact all-in Volibear wants: Feint (W) absorbs incoming damage for a few seconds right when Q's stun and W's mark would land, and Shadow Dash (E) taunts Volibear into a fight on Shen's terms instead of yours. With no ranged burst to punish through the shield, Shen dictates engages, which lines up with his lane and solo-kill advantage and Volibear's 32.7% win rate over 147 games.

theirWindow.when: Shadow Dash (E) is up and he's near
theirWindow.what: He can dash in, taunt you, and trade Vorpal Blade (Q) on his terms. Back off the wave rather than standing in his 575-range dash threat.

yourWindow.what: Its 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown means there's a real window with no shield. Commit Q (Thundering Smash) into double-cast W (Frenzied Maul) now, not before.

start.why: The 34.6% win rate path over 130 games; the extra sustain lets you sit on poke exchanges without needing to force a kill into an up Feint.

boots.why: 35.3% win rate over 51 games, and the tenacity directly cuts the duration of the one hard-CC tool Shen uses to control your engages: the Shadow Dash taunt.

core.why: First item in the 30% win rate core path; gets you online for sustained trading rather than one burst window.
Keeps your ability haste and attack speed scaling so W (Frenzied Maul) and E (Sky Splitter) come back fast enough to out-poke his cooldown-reliant kit.
Caps the core path; the extra healing amplifies Frenzied Maul's self-heal on the double-cast.

situational.when: you're ahead and need wave clear to punish his split-push tendencies
the game goes long and you need extra sustain and poke damage in extended trades
his team stacks tanky frontline and you need true damage to break through

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping attack speed rewards the sustained, wait-it-out trading this matchup demands instead of a single burst window Feint can just absorb.

summoners.why: Flash + Exhaust posts the best measured win rate (37.5%) and directly answers his Shadow Dash engage and Ki Strike burst when he does commit; Flash + Teleport is the more popular, safer pick (31.3% win rate, 18.1% pick rate) if you'd rather prioritize wave resets over a hard counter to his all-in.

playing.title: Wait for Feint to be down
playing.detail: Only commit Q (Thundering Smash) into your all-in once you've seen Shen use W (Feint). Its 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown gives you a clear window where there's no shield for your burst.

playing.title: Poke with Sky Splitter
playing.detail: Use E (Sky Splitter) at its 1200 range to chip Shen without walking into Shadow Dash range. Standing in your own blast grants a shield, so you can poke and soak at the same time.

playing.title: Respect the taunt dash
playing.detail: Shadow Dash (E) taunts anyone it hits and its cooldown drops as low as 8s at max rank. Back off the wave when it's up instead of standing in his 575-range dash threat.

playing.title: Double-tap Frenzied Maul
playing.detail: Land W (Frenzied Maul) twice on the same target for bonus damage and a heal. This sustained-damage pattern beats his shield better than any single burst attempt.

playing.title: Don't facilitate Vorpal Blade heals
playing.detail: Shen's Q (Vorpal Blade) life-taps him on cast and heals any ally who then attacks the marked target. Be extra cautious trading into it when his jungler is nearby, not just in isolated 1v1s.

playing.title: Save R for a real dive
playing.detail: Stormbringer (R) only returns every 160-110s and disables nearby towers on landing. Hold it for a forced dive window post-6 rather than trying to force a lane kill his kit is built to deny.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, summoner spells, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the cooldown-window reasoning and trade patterns are my own analysis layered on top of the ability text.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid Shen’s taunt. Avoid using your [Q][W] while Shen’s (W) is active. Use [E] to contest lane and wait for a chance.
